question: Commercialisation of agriculture is an indication of _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Marketable surplus.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Commercialisation of agriculture** refers to the process of **transforming agriculture **from a subsistence-based activity to a commercial enterprise.
 
• This involves producing **crops and goods **not only for personal consumption but also for **sale in the market.**
 
• When agriculture is commercialised, there is an increase in **marketable surplus, **which is the amount of agricultural produce that is available for sale in the market after meeting the **needs of the producers** and their families.
 
• This surplus can be sold for a** profit,** leading to an **increase in income** for the farmers.
 
• **Producers' surplus** refers to the** difference **between the price at which the producer is willing to sell a product and the **actual price** they receive in the market.
 
 
• This surplus is** maximised **when the producer is able to sell their product at a** higher price** than their cost of production.
 
 
 
• **Consumer surplus** refers to the difference between the price that **consumers are willing to pay** for a product and the actual price they pay.
 
 
• This surplus is maximised when the price of the product is **lower **than the value that consumers place on it.
 
 
 
• **Income surplus** refers to the **increase in income** that is generated as a result of commercialisation of agriculture.
 
 
• This surplus is maximised when the marketable surplus is sold at a price that is** higher than the cost of production.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The term 'commercialisation of agriculture' is often associated with the **Green Revolution**, which was a period of significant agricultural innovation and productivity growth that occurred in the **1960s and 1970s.**
 
• The Green Revolution involved the introduction of **new crop varieties, improved irrigation systems**, and the **use of fertilisers and pesticides.**
 
• These innovations led to a significant increase in **agricultural productivity** and helped to** alleviate food shortages **in many parts of the world.
 
• However, there are also concerns about the **negative environmental **and **social impacts **of commercialisation of agriculture, such as **soil degradation, water pollution,** and displacement of** small-scale farmers.**
 
• In addition to marketable surplus, commercialisation of agriculture can also lead to the** emergence of agribusinesses**, which are large-scale, commercial enterprises that are involved in various aspects of agriculture, such as** production, processing, and distribution.**
